CPolicy Guidelines

A. Purpose: To provide guideline instruction for prevention of infant abductions and ensure proper safety to the newborns.

B.Scope : All infants’ patients born in the hospital.

C. Policy Guidelines:

1. Facility Security Safeguards:

  • Labour room is equipped with self-closing, locking doors. The access privilege to the labour room is given only to authorized staff of the hospital
  • The hospital does not include a dedicated nursery hence preventing chances of infant swapping
  • The Security guards checks the mother and the infant and verifies the identification bands & the discharge ticket before they are allowed to be discharged from the hospital

2. Work Practices for Safeguarding Infants and Children:

  • The hospital staff in the maternity, labour room are trained and educated about the policy & procedures for preventing infant & child abduction
  • The mother is educated and counseled about safety measures & precautions to be taken to prevent infant abduction
  • Identification bands are attached to the infant
  • Footprints of the infant are imprinted on the best side tickets which is attested by the duty doctor
  • A full physical assessment of the infant is done after birth or admission and documented in the case file
  • The Birth certificate contains information pertaining to newborn like its parent’s names and address, date and time of birth.
  • The infants are kept in direct, line-of-site supervision at all times by a authorized staff member& the mother
  • In case the patient is referred to any other clinical specialty, the security guard on duty will allow shifting of the patient only after checking the “refer slip” duly filled and signed by the concerned doctor. The security guard verifies the details mentioned in the refer slip with those indicated in the identification band.
  • The infants are transported only by authorized staff.
  • Other hospitals in the area are alerted of any suspicious person as a preventive proactive measure
  • The parents are explained and advised to supervise their children at all times in waiting rooms and outpatient clinics.

Code Pink Process:

1. Purpose

To establish a standardized procedure for immediate response and management of suspected or confirmed child/infant abduction, ensuring rapid action, safety, and recovery.

2. Scope

Applicable to:

  • Labour Room
  • Maternity Ward
  • OPD / Waiting Areas
  • All hospital staff, security personnel, and administration

3. Definition

Code Pink: A hospital emergency code activated in case of suspected or confirmed infant/child abduction or missing child.

4. Responsibilities

Nursing Staff

  • Immediate identification of missing infant/child
  • Activate Code Pink
  • Inform nursing supervisor

Security Staff

  • Initiate lockdown of all entry/exit points
  • Monitor CCTV and restrict movement

Medical Officer / Consultant

  • Supervise clinical area
  • Support communication and documentation

Hospital Administration

  • Inform police and higher authorities
  • Coordinate external communication

5. Procedure (Step-by-Step Response)

Step 1: Identification

  • Any staff noticing missing infant/child must:
    • Confirm with mother/guardian
    • Check nearby areas immediately

Step 2: Code Activation

  • Announce loudly or via intercom:
    “Code Pink, Code Pink – [Location”
  • Inform:
    • Nursing Station
    • Security Control Room
    • Hospital Administration

Step 3: Immediate Lockdown

  • Security to:
    • Close all gates, lifts, staircases
    • Restrict entry/exit of all persons
    • Deploy guards at all exits

Step 4: Search Operation

  • Divide staff into teams:
    • Ward search
    • Corridor & washroom check
    • Parking & hospital premises

Step 5: CCTV Surveillance

  • Security team to:
    • Review real-time CCTV footage
    • Track suspicious movement
    • Identify suspect description

Step 6: Verification

  • Check:
    • Infant identification bands
    • Discharge slips
    • Authorization of any person carrying a baby

Step 7: External Communication

  • Inform:
    • Local Police immediately
    • Nearby hospitals (alert system)
  • Provide:
    • Infant details
    • Suspect description

Step 8: Documentation

  • Record:
    • Time of incident
    • Staff involved
    • Actions taken
  • Prepare incident report

Step 9: Deactivation

  • Code Pink is closed only after:
    • Infant/child is located safely OR
    • Police take over investigation
